entities.summary: Joseph Ernest Renan was a French Orientalist and Semitic scholar, writing on Semitic languages and civilizations, historian of religion, philologist, philosopher, biblical scholar, and critic. He wrote works on the origins of early Christianity, and espoused popular political theories especially concerning nationalism, national identity, and the superiority of white people over other human races. Renan is among the first scholars to advance the debunked Khazar theory, which held that Ashkenazi Jews were descendants of the Khazars, Turkic peoples who had adopted the Jewish religion and allegedly migrated to central and eastern Europe following the collapse of their khanate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Renan's works on Semitic languages and civilizations contributed to a greater understanding of Jewish history and identity, while his nationalist theories had significant regional implications in Western Europe. His ideas on the origins of early Christianity also shaped biblical scholarship.
